contents.name: Periodic residual and initial-defect formulation
contents.support: Source context for defining a continuous PDE residual and initial defect. The local Definition fixes the periodic torus and Fourier projector explicitly.

contents.name: Smooth solution comparison under forcing difference
contents.support: Supports the energy-method route for a smooth exact solution compared with a smooth surrogate viewed as a solution with forcing shifted by its residual. The local proof supplies the exact periodic projected calculation and sharper time-weighted formula.

sources.locator: Definition 3.4 and §§4.1–4.5, especially Lemmas 4.1–4.3 and Proposition 4.5: residual/datum errors, error differential inequality, comparison, and a posteriori bound.

contents.name: Definition 3.4 continuous differential residual and datum error
contents.support: Defines a continuous periodic differential residual and initial-data defect for a smooth approximate solution; the local Definition gives the exact L1-time/L2-space norm.

contents.name: §4 error equation, norm inequality, and comparison theorem
contents.support: The complete relevant proof derives the error equation, handles zero and nonzero error norms, compares the scalar control inequality, and concludes a conditional error bound. Its higher Sobolev regularity and existence conclusion are not imported.

contents.support: Provides the Cauchy–Schwarz special case used to combine the training-law L2 state error with the L2 density bound. The distribution-shift estimate itself is proved locally.

contents.reason: The finite measure example does not assume invariant conditional labels or analyze a reweighted empirical-risk estimator; the identity is context only.

source_review.read_extent: Inspected the complete target-risk identity and its covariate-shift premise in §3.7.3.1.
source_review.supports: The target-risk reweighting formula requires a source-to-target density ratio under the stated covariate-shift model.
source_review.limitations: This learning-theory identity is not used to prove the example, which is checked directly on a two-point measurable space.

contents.name: §3.7.3.1 and Exercise 2(b–c): support overlap and the infinite-weight case
contents.support: The source states that a target point with positive mass and zero source probability has an infinite importance ratio. The Example directly realizes the support failure with μ=δ₀ and ν=δ₁, then proves ν is not absolutely continuous with respect to μ; no algorithmic result is imported.

source_review.read_extent: Inspected the complete support-overlap caveat at the end of §3.7.3.1 and Exercise 2(b–c), which ask for the finite-ratio support condition and the omitted target-risk region.
source_review.supports: A target-supported input missing from the source support cannot receive a finite source-based importance weight.
source_review.limitations: The text discusses density-based learning distributions; the finite counterexample is established independently for arbitrary probability measures.

sources.title: Masashi Sugiyama, Matthias Krauledat, and Klaus-Robert Müller, “Covariate Shift Adaptation by Importance Weighted Cross Validation”
sources.locator: Complete §2.1, printed pp. 986–987 / PDF pp. 2–3: training and test input laws, covariate-shift setup, and the finite, known density-ratio assumption in equation (3).

contents.name: §2.1: test/training law mismatch and finite-known density-ratio premise
contents.support: The paper explicitly assumes a finite, known test-to-training density ratio at training inputs. The Example isolates the boundary where the target law places all mass outside the training law, so no Radon–Nikodym density exists; this is a local finite counterexample, not a result claimed from the paper.

source_review.read_extent: Inspected the full §2.1 setup, definitions of training/test risk, covariate-shift premise, density ratio equation (3), and the stated finite-known-ratio assumption.
source_review.supports: The example’s warning that a target-law guarantee needs a density-ratio condition is consistent with the paper’s explicit assumptions.
source_review.limitations: The paper treats Euclidean input densities and statistical model-selection procedures; it does not state the finite Dirac-law counterexample or prove the local estimate.
